    How to use your Money Tracker

    Step by step, with pictures. The screenshots show an example person, Aina. The orange numbers in each picture match the list under it.

    0The idea in one minute

    Money comes insalary, gift, side income
    →
    Split into 3 potsSpend 60% · Save 20% · Invest 20%
    →
    You log what you usemeals, spending, savings, investments
    →
    You always knowyour total balance and what is left in each pot

    Total balance = all money in − all spending (food + other). Money moved into savings or investments is still yours, so it stays inside your total balance.

    What you need: this one file, Money_Tracker_App.html, opened in Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer. No Excel, no internet, no account. Your entries are saved in a data file on your own computer.
    Part 1 · Start (once, 2 minutes)

    1Create your data file

    1. Make a folder for your money stuff, e.g. Documents\Money, and put Money_Tracker_App.html in it.
    2. Double-click the file to open it in Chrome or Edge.
    1. First time? Create my data file – a save window opens. Choose your Money folder and click Save. A file called money-data.json is created. From now on every entry is saved there automatically.
    2. I already have a data file – use this on a new computer, or after reinstalling, to continue with your existing money-data.json.
    Tip: put the folder inside OneDrive or Google Drive – your data file is then backed up automatically.

    2Quick setup

    1. Your name – shown at the top of the app.
    2. Daily food budget – how much you allow yourself for food per day, e.g. 20.
    3. Money split – Spend / Save / Invest in %. Must add up to 100. 60 / 20 / 20 is a good start. Spend covers bills, transport, food and fun.
    4. Money you have today – add up your bank accounts, e-wallets and cash. This becomes your Starting balance.
    5. Start tracking – done!
    Part 2 · Every day (1 minute)

    3The Home screen

    1. Save status – a green dot and "Saved to money-data.json" means your entries are safe in your file.
    2. Messages – what to do next. Green = fine, yellow = something to do (e.g. "Move RM 910 into your savings"), red = a problem.
    3. Key numbers – total balance, what's left to spend, still to save, ready to invest, food today, and how much you can spend on food per day for the rest of the month.
    4. + Add – this button is always in the bottom-right corner. Use it to add anything.
    5. Total net worth – one point per day. Hover over the line to see the balance and what happened that day.

    4Add a meal (or anything else)

    Click + Add. The same window adds meals, spending, money in, savings and investments.

    1. Type – choose what you're adding: Meal, Spending, Money in, Savings or Investment.
    2. Date – today is filled in. Change it if you're adding something from another day.
    3. Meal – Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner or Snacks (drinks count as snacks). It guesses from the time of day.
    4. What did you eat? – e.g. nasi lemak 7. Put the price at the end and it moves into the price box by itself. Meals you've had before are suggested as you type.
    5. Amount – the price. 0 if it was free. You can type sums like 8+2.5.
    6. Save & add another – saves and opens a new empty form, handy for logging the whole day at once. Save just saves and closes.
    Made a mistake? Every list has ✎ (edit) and 🗑 (delete). After deleting, an Undo button appears for a few seconds.

    5The Food page

    1. Month – choose which month to look at.
    2. + Add meal – same as the + Add button.
    3. Month summary – spent, budget, saved or over, average per day, days over budget, most expensive day.
    4. Every day – blue bar = within budget, red bar = over, dashed line = your daily budget. Hover over a bar to see what you ate.
    1. Each day – the date, Within or Over, and the day's total.
    2. ✎ / 🗑 – edit or delete a meal.
    3. Search your meals – type e.g. bubble tea to see how often you had it and how much it cost in total.

    6Spending – everything that is not a meal

    Groceries, bills, petrol, phone plan, rent, shopping, movies… Click + Add → Spending, choose a category, type the amount and a short note.

    1. + Add spending – add a payment.
    2. Month – one month, or "All time".
    3. By category – which categories cost the most. Scroll down for the full list of payments with ✎ / 🗑.
    Food or Spending? Meals and drinks you eat → Meal. Groceries you cook with → Spending (Groceries).
    Part 3 · Now and then

    7Money In – when you receive money

    Salary, bonus, side income, angpao, refunds: click + Add → Money in. Use the amount that actually reached you (salary after EPF / SOCSO / tax).

    1. + Add money in.
    2. Totals – everything received, this month, and how much each pot has received.
    3. Each entry – with its split into Spend / Save / Invest.

    8Savings & goals

    When you actually move money into a savings account or fixed deposit, add it here. Type a minus amount (e.g. -200) when you take money out.

    1. + New goal – e.g. "Emergency fund", target RM 6,000, by 31 Dec 2027.
    2. + Add savings – record money you moved, and choose which goal it's for.
    3. Goal card – saved so far, % reached, and how much to save per month to reach it on time.
    4. Savings log – every entry, with ✎ / 🗑.

    9Investments

    1. + Add investment – where (ASNB, Stocks, Gold…) and how much. A minus amount = you withdrew money.
    2. Totals – the Invest pot, how much you invested, what's still ready to invest, and the current value.
    3. Current value – optional. Now and then, check your investment app and type today's value to see your gain or loss.
    Part 4 · Check your money

    10Pots – your total balance and the 3 pots

    1. Messages – what to do next.
    2. Spend / Save / Invest – what's left in each pot. The bar shows how much is used; red means over.
    3. Your total balance – money in minus food and other spending. Should be close to the real money in your accounts.
    4. Where your balance is – cash for spending, cash waiting to be saved or invested, and what's already in savings and investments.

    Further down, This month shows the same for the current month only: if "Spend share left this month" is red, this month's spending is bigger than this month's income share.

    11Net worth

    1. Range – last month, 6 months, 1 year or everything.
    2. Changes – now, last 30 days, last 12 months, and your highest ever.
    3. Daily line – end-of-day balance. Flat parts are days with no money in or out. Further down: money in vs spent per month, and month-end balances.
    Part 5 · Your data

    12Settings & your data file

    1. Daily food budget – change it any time; the new budget applies from today, past days keep the old one. Click Save.
    2. Money split – change the % (must total 100). It applies from today; past income keeps its old split.
    3. Dropdown lists – the choices for sources, categories, investment places and savings. One per line – add your own, e.g. "Parents allowance".
    4. Your data file – which file is used and when it was last saved, plus:
      • Export to Excel – a spreadsheet of everything (for your own analysis or printing).
      • Download backup (.json) – an extra copy of your data file.
      • Open another data file / Save to a new file – switch or move your data.
      • Import from Money_Tracker_Template.xlsx – bring in entries from the Excel version of the tracker.

    13Next time you open the app

    The app remembers your data file and shows your entries straight away. For your safety, Chrome / Edge may ask once per visit before the app can save into the file again:

    1. Reconnect – click it, and click Allow / Edit files in the browser's question. That's it.
    2. When the status turns green ("Saved to money-data.json"), everything is saved again.
    Firefox or Safari? They can't save to a file directly. The app still works, but your entries are kept inside that browser only. Click Download data file regularly – or use Chrome / Edge.
    Cheat-sheet

    Your routine at a glance

    WhenDo this
    After every meal (or once in the evening)+ Add → Meal → what + price
    You pay for something+ Add → Spending → category + amount
    Money comes in+ Add → Money in → source + amount
    You move money to savings+ Add → Savings → goal + amount
    You invest+ Add → Investment → where + amount
    Once a weekRead the messages on Home, move money if it says so
    Once a monthSettings → Download backup

    Questions & fixes

    Where exactly is my data?

    In the money-data.json file you created (see Settings → Your data file). A copy is also kept inside your browser as a safety net. Nothing is sent anywhere.

    Can I open the data file in Excel?

    Use Settings → Export to Excel – it creates a proper spreadsheet with all your entries. Don't edit the .json file by hand.

    My total balance doesn't match my bank.

    Usually a payment wasn't logged, or the starting balance was off. Find the difference and add it as Spending, or as Money in with source "Other" and the note "adjustment".

    "Left to spend" is red.

    You've spent more than your Spend share, so the extra is coming out of money meant for saving or investing. Spend less for a while, or raise the Spend % in Settings if your bills really need more.

    "Ready to invest" is negative.

    You invested more than your Invest share. Pause investing until new income tops the pot up.

    I use two computers.

    Keep the data file in OneDrive / Google Drive and open the same file on both computers (I already have a data file). Don't have the app open on both at the same time.

    The status says "Not saved to file".

    Click it (or the Reconnect button) and allow the browser to edit the file. If the file was moved or renamed, use Settings → Open another data file.

    I deleted something by mistake.

    Click Undo right away. If it's too late, just add it again.

    Can I use it on my phone?

    The app is designed to also fit a phone screen, but saving to a file only works in Chrome / Edge on a computer. On a phone, entries would stay inside the phone's browser.

    I was using the Excel tracker before.

    Settings → Import from Money_Tracker_Template.xlsx brings in your money in, meals, spending, savings, investments, food budget and split.

    Everything runs inside your browser. Nothing is uploaded, and it works offline.
